chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:

I asked him about a man placing his hand on the grave, what is it and why did he do it? So he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did it upon his son after sprinkling (water). I asked him how I should place my hand on the graves of the Muslims, so he gestured with his hand to the ground and placed it upon it, then raised it, and he was facing the Qiblah.
ai.seo_question: What is the ritual significance and method of placing a hand on a grave in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Aban ibn Taghlib, establishes the Sunnah of touching the grave as a gesture of intimacy and confirmation of the burial site, specifically citing the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) action upon his son. The physical description of gesturing to the earth while facing the Qiblah underscores the ritual's orientation towards divine direction, reflecting the Shia emphasis on following the Prophet's familial and practical precedents in funeral rites.
